pr_body:
Implements a native clipboard interface API for Lua, fixes #2073

```lua
-- Empties the clipboard
app.clipboard.clear()

-- Content check
app.clipboard.hasText
app.clipboard.hasImage

-- Quick access
app.clipboard.text
app.clipboard.image

-- Full table
app.clipboard.content = {
 image,
 selection,
 palette,
 tileset,
 text
}
```
pr_comments:
I'll take a look right now...

> do we want to prompt or at least notify the user that a script has read their clipboard? Having a permission for it maybe?

Yes, we should require a prompt/security flag for this specific permission (when image or text is read/get from the clipboard).

Added the security prompt and implemented the changes:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e025709e-7f3b-4057-81ca-376469b5ca53)

I noticed that it was flagging my script as "internal" on the first instance of the script requesting acccess, which I'm not entirely sure why it happens, I can probably take a better look at the logic and UI behind this when tackling #4739.
It was also saying "nternal" because the text was getting +1'd for some reason? Unclear why that was there and the git blame was not particularly illuminating since it's always been like this.

I also changed `isText` and `isImage` to `hasText` and `hasImage`, which I think makes more sense if you want to use it like `app.clipboard.content.text` in that case you can check beforehand if "content" has text, semantically it tracks better in my brain.

Testing it with a normal script its working fine but the test is failing for some reason, I'll take a look at later but figured I'd push the changes in case there's any more feedback.

Renamed "mask" to "selection" since that's what it's known as in scripting, API now looks like:

```lua
-- Empties the clipboard
app.clipboard.clear()

-- Content check
app.clipboard.hasText
app.clipboard.hasImage

-- Quick access
app.clipboard.text
app.clipboard.image

-- Full table
app.clipboard.content = {
 image,
 selection,
 palette,
 tileset,
 text
}
```

I was wondering: Do we need hasText & hasImage when now app.clipboard.text && app.clipboard.image return `nil` instead of failing when they get called? I think they're kinda redundant.

We could also add a helper to copy the current sprite to the clipboard with all the data we can have (custom format, etc) since the way to do it right now is slightly cumbersome, like:
```lua
app.clipboard.content = {
    image = app.image,
    palettte = sprite.palettes[1],
    selection = sprite.selection,
    tileset = app.layer.tileset
  }
```

could become:
```lua
app.clipboard.copyActive() 
``` 
or something like that, maybe? Just an idea.

I've tested with a script like:
```lua
app.clipboard.clear()
```
And I found strange that it asked permission to read the clipboard (when we're writing it/ clearing its content).

What do you think? Should we ask for `CLIPBOARD_GATE(FileAccessMode::Write);` for these cases (clear/set_image/set_text/set_content)?

Hm, yeah, reading permission makes sense but write permission could be annoying - personally I like when software explicit tells me it's gonna mess with my clipboard (I have my phone set to tell me whenever my clipboard changes) so for me it seemed reasonable but for a regular user it might be unnecessary and unwelcome. It's up to what you think is the most consistent with how the rest of the API behaves wrt system access.

issue_context.title: Lua:  Clipboard access in the commands API
issue_context.body:
1.- It would be great having access to the clipboard in the API like:

app.command.PasteClipboardText

It would allow to create third party interaction inside Aseprite.

2.- And adding custom keyboard shortcuts for scripts would be also a great feature

Aseprite v1.2.11 and above.
